item.title: 8 Weeks
item.description:
8 weeks in. I’ve made amazing progress. Unfortunately I haven’t kept up with this site. Here’s a quick recap of the past 5 weeks:

  • Week 5: I started with my new strategy and solved about 20 problems. I was feeling reat.
  • Week 6: I started to dream up an even better strategy. I sunk some time into planning it out. The goal was to move even faster, generate more answers (on appraoch, outline, and actual code) with AI, then do a very thorough review.
  • Week 7: Some big distractions. I joined a new team for my job, and this just happend to come with the assignment of learning a new programming language. This was a blessing and a curse. Of course it was the perfect assignment for me, but it also split my effort.
  • Week 8: Family visitng town. This always takes away from side-pursuits like this.

Needless to say, I’ve been busy. But I’ve also managed to keep my focus, and despite some fluctuations in velocity, I’m still moving forward.

item.title: Recapping and resetting my strategy
item.description:
I’m 3 weeks in to my coding journey. It’s been a blast so far. Robert Frost had some line about “Making my advocation my vocation”. It’s great when you find something in life that you’re so excited about you want to give your all to it.

After 3 weeks I had solved a whopping 45 leetcode problems. I could tell I was into it. Being a noobie, obviously I was using a lot of resources, especially AI, to help.

item.title: Blogging my journey
item.description:
About a week into my code learning journey I got a tip from a friend. He shared his repo where he’d stored all his leetcode solutions. This was brilliant. The site itself is pretty easy to use, but taking the time to copy out my solutions, then work through commenting them, and saving them somewhere I could share? A no brainer.

After setting up my own repo of solutions it dawned on me: I might like to write a bit about my journey. I’m sure no one will read it. All the better. The internet needs more personal websites.

item.title: Learning to code
item.description:
On the last day of January this year I set out to learn to code. This is not the first time I’ve been down this path. But… the stars aligned and I got a very helpful email from a friend who set me on my way.

The email? It mentioned 2 important things:

  • nothing beats hard work
  • try out leetcode

Hard work. Really? Wait. I always thought of coding and software as producing “smart solutions”. Whereas, I chalked up myself and my approaches as hardway, slow, inferior. I don’t know why (lack of brain cells), but I never sat down and gave learning to code an honest days hard work. It’s funny how a quick mention can have a huge impact.
